findings.description: The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no separate encryption resource visible), so objects such as the customer master file are stored unencrypted.

No ACL is set to private and no public access block / bucket policy restricting public access is declared; the in-code comment confirms the bucket is intended to be public, exposing sensitive customer data to anonymous readers.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads and writes to sensitive data are not auditable, hindering detection of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrites or deletions (including malicious ones, made easier by force_destroy = true) are unrecoverable.

A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible aws_s3_bucket.data without specifying kms_key_id or server-side encryption, exposing sensitive customer data.
The financials bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so financial records are stored in cleartext at rest.
No logging block is configured, leaving access to financial data unaudited despite a logs bucket existing in the file.
Although the ACL is private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, so a later bucket policy or ACL change could inadvertently expose financial data publicly.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, meaning financial objects can be permanently deleted with no recovery or integrity trail.

The operations bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption. Any data placed here is unprotected at rest relative to the other buckets in this file.

No logging block is configured for the operations bucket, so object-level access to it is not recorded to the logs bucket, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorised access or exfiltration.

The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no bucket policy denying public access, so a later ACL or policy change could silently make the bucket and its objects publicly readable.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest, unlike the logs bucket which uses SSE-KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy accompanies this bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth guard against accidental public ACLs or policies being applied to it later.

The central log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no policy denying public or unencrypted (non-TLS) access, so audit logs could be exposed by a subsequent ACL/policy misconfiguration.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, so log data can be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections to S3.
